Initial evaluation includes A1c, urine albumin-creatinine ratio, lipid panel, renal ultrasound, serum electrolytes, urinalysis, and urine microscopy.
For CKD with hypertension or diabetes, use ACE/ARB and titrate to maximally tolerated dose for renal protection, monitoring potassium (hold if >5.5) and GFR (discontinue if drop >30%).
Finerenone (a nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist) reduces sustained GFR decline and risk of ESRD in stage 3-4 CKD.
Lifestyle interventions: plant-based diet, protein 0.6-0.8 g/kg/day for stage 3-4, 150 min/week moderate exercise, resistance training to prevent sarcopenia, and tobacco cessation.
Statins are recommended for cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD regardless of kidney protection.
In CKD with diabetes, target A1c 6.5-8% depending on life situation and use SGLT2 inhibitors and metformin.

Refer to nephrology for hematuria, hereditary kidney disease, approaching ESRD, nephrotic syndrome, rapidly progressive disease, severe electrolyte abnormalities, structural abnormalities, or uncontrolled hypertension.
